title: QUIC RFC 9000 S19P20 HANDSHAKE_DONE Proof Tail
purpose: Describe the focused S19P20 HANDSHAKE_DONE closure for frame type encoding, server-only send gating, completion timing, and server receipt error handling.
design_summary: HANDSHAKE_DONE remains a fixed QUIC frame type parsed and formatted through the shared frame codec as the single-byte varint value 0x1e. The runtime emits the frame only from the server role, only after the peer handshake transcript completion path promotes the connection to active, and only once per connection. Application Data packet receive dispatch treats a HANDSHAKE_DONE frame received by a server as a local PROTOCOL_VIOLATION close while non-HANDSHAKE_DONE protected frames continue through ordinary receive handling.
data_and_state_considerations: The closure relies on existing runtime state: tlsState.Role gates server-only send and receive policy, peerHandshakeTranscriptCompleted gates the completion boundary, handshakeDonePacketSent prevents duplicate sends, and tracked sent packet plaintext payload metadata provides direct requirement-home proof of the emitted frame.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The frame codec rejects adjacent single-byte frame types and non-minimal two-byte varint encodings of value 0x1e.
A valid HANDSHAKE_DONE frame consumes exactly one type byte when another frame follows in the same payload.
An active client runtime with a completed peer handshake transcript does not emit HANDSHAKE_DONE.
A server with 1-RTT send material still does not emit HANDSHAKE_DONE before peer handshake transcript completion.
Repeated completion signals do not duplicate the HANDSHAKE_DONE send.
A server receiving a protected HANDSHAKE_DONE closes with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION while a protected PING packet does not take that close path.
risks: This slice does not claim broad frame-dispatch completeness beyond the focused S19P20 HANDSHAKE_DONE path.
This slice does not widen public APIs for observing or controlling HANDSHAKE_DONE.
This slice does not claim hosted interop readiness.
This slice does not close unrelated deferred fuzz obligations.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the focused S19P20 hard proof tail for REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S19P20-0003 through REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-1372. It does not claim broader S19 frame-family closure, public API widening, hosted interop readiness, or closure of unrelated deferred fuzz obligations.
